body:
I will add that I'm wondering if this is related to this old Go bug (at least as it related to os.rename() behavior on Windows):

https://github.com/golang/go/issues/8914

If there is an open file handle in `.../wal.tmp/`, that would block an OS-level rename from working.
@MartyMacGyver Maybe you can give a try to fix?

I'm limited in what I can contribute to a project like this employer-wise.

But to discuss it...

First, while the other bug I mentioned above may be useful to refer to, this isn't quite the same problem.

Second, if there was a test that executes the "new install" case without a default.etcd folder, that would reproduce and flag this error.

In wal.go:105 (Create()), the WAL file gets locked (from fileutil/lock_windows.go, we see this uses LOCKFILE_EXCLUSIVE_LOCK). Then later in the function, the folder containing this locked file gets renamed. That fails as a contained file is locked.

This (new in v3) attempt to make Create() appear atomic goes a bit too far, at least for operability on Windows. Specifically, creating a temp folder, exclusively locking a file within it, and then trying to rename that folder, isn't going to work on Windows. I'm not sure what the architectural imperative is for this enhanced atomicity in v3. Perhaps some junction manipulation would work (at least in NTFS), but exclusively locking the file and renaming its containing folder isn't going to work - perhaps one must simply abstract a relaxed requirement for Windows, much like multiple lock_\* abstractions exist for lock functionality, or accept deprecated functionality by effectively disallowing the initialization without manual intervention.

I prefer to see the former, even if it means accepting that Windows can't mimic atomicity for this use case, or at best using some other mechanism (e.g., MoveFileEx) to better handle this case. However, it might mean some re-architecture of this: I'm not sure why the temp folder is getting renamed, versus a temp file (via MoveFileEx if in Windows, to preserve posix-style behavior - see the above-referenced bug for more on that topic).
One additional note: this use of os.Rename() as part of the atomic WAL folder init is part of a relatively recent change via commit e6add51, fixing bug #5270.

@MartyMacGyver there are multiple files in the directory; if etcd is killed in the middle of init without atomic rename of the directory then it could have a partially initialized wal directory (which came up in stress testing). I believe the fix is to hold off on locking until after the rename. I'll see if I can get it working again.
